notes:
Account snapshot - quick bullets and raw CRM notes:
- Company: mid-market B2B SaaS (workflow automation) with aggressive roadmap to ship generative chat assistant in Q3.
- Primary driver: user-facing chat agents with tool calling (calendar/CRM actions) + streaming partial responses for snappy UX.
- Reported problem: "incumbent has had latency regressions since Dec; streaming responses often stall at token 1->5 for 95p, hurting perceived speed". Quote from Head of Product: "Users think the assistant is slow — even when avg latency is OK, the stream start is inconsistent."
- SLO targets: initial token/first-byte streaming <=200ms p95, sustained token latency ~10-20ms/token; throughput target 50-120 rps during peak. Cost-sensitive but will pay for predictable latency.
- Model preference: open model (LLM variants) acceptable; want Redwood-verified performance profile + fallback to smaller model for low-pri queries.
- Interested in Hosted API to validate streaming & tool-calling, then migrate to Dedicated for predictable tail latency and capacity isolation.
- Security asks: SSO (SAML), 1y audit logs, KMS integration for keys, NA data residency.
- POC scope: 72-hour side-by-side streaming benchmark against incumbent (same prompts, same infra region), include tool-calling latency (end-to-end from client event to tool return), and token-level latency traces. SE to run and provide artifact with p50/p95/p99, byte-to-first-token timing, streaming continuity metric.
- Pricing: asked for committed reserved capacity tiers and burst policy; procurement wants 12mo committed quote + breakout for hosted fallback.
- Contacts: Head of Product - Maya Gonzalez (m.gonzalez@orchidhalo.ai), Platform Eng lead - Samir Rao.
- Open links: drive pricing deck (shared 02/05), security FAQ (sent 02/05), Fireflies calls for demos (ff_20260214_01).
- Quote from Product: "If Redwood can beat their streaming start/continuity we'll migrate; happy to take pricing for Dedicated once POC validates tail latency."
- Risks: incumbent early-termination, legal SLA reqs for data residency, and need to demonstrate consistent multi-region fallbacks.
